relations.myth: Ngünechen sends Filew to sustain the succession of machi
relations.note: Filew acts as Ngünechen’s Spirit of Power and Wisdom.

relations.myth: Filew and Ngünechen merge in some practitioners’ accounts
relations.note: Recent ritual testimony sometimes identifies Filew with Ngünechen and sometimes distinguishes them.

relations.myth: Generic and individual machi spirits overlap contextually
relations.note: Filew may coincide with machi püllü or remain the generic ancestral spirit.

relations.myth: Ngen selects machi and delegates power through Filew
relations.note: Regional testimony links tutelary ngen with Filew in selecting and empowering practitioners.

relations.myth: Filew empowers healing against harmful wekufü possession
relations.note: Filew enables the machi to identify, negotiate with, or expel harmful wekufü.
relations.source: Foerster, Introducción a la religiosidad mapuche

relations.myth: Filew counters harmful forces sent through kalku sorcery
relations.note: Filew empowers diagnosis and resistance against attacks attributed to a kalku.

relations.myth: Filew belongs to the ancestral upper-world spirit complex
relations.note: Filew is associated with ancestral sky spirits and may arrive from wenu mapu.
Christian-influenced theology analogizes Filew, Ngünechen’s Spirit of Power and Wisdom, to the Holy Spirit.
